text:
Ava (PM): FYI — FinCo (pilot prospect) pushed an RFP this morning. They want: per-tenant capacity controls, model routing by latency tier, and an SLA for 99.9% inference availability. Sales wants a ship/no-ship call by EOD tomorrow.

Maya (Sales): They said pricing is secondary to reliability. Quote: 'If you can match our latency profiles and guarantee isolation, we can move to an enterprise contract.' They asked for an implementation timeline — can we give 6–8 weeks?

Raj (Eng): 6–8 weeks is optimistic. Per-tenant capacity + routing needs changes in scheduling and governance. Roughly: 2 weeks design, 3–4 weeks infra + runtime changes, 1–2 weeks e2e tests. Risk: Dedicated autoscaling overlaps with this work.

Liam (SE): For the pilot we can propose a scoped MVP:
```
MVP acceptance criteria:\n- Per-tenant GPU caps (soft limits) + overprovision alerting
- Routing policy with two latency tiers (low/standard) + fallback
- Audit log for model selection events
- Degraded-mode behavior documented
```
If we keep quantization/advanced batching out of scope it's faster.

Priya (CS): Also important: FinCo needs auditability for compliance. If we can't promise full dedicated isolation they want signed SOC2 control mapping. Might affect deal timeline.

Noah (Design): UI ask from prospect: simple toggle for capacity caps and a latency-tier selector in the console. Can ship a basic form and iterate; don't need polished UX for pilot.

Jordan (CTO): Two framing questions: 1) Is this a one-off enterprise ask (big ACV) or a platform-level signal? 2) If we prioritize this, what do we deprioritize? We can't do everything.

Ava (PM): It's both — big chance for a logo + it surfaces platform gaps we already logged. Proposal: scoped MVP for the pilot (Liam's acceptance criteria) + a temporary routing shim for hosted customers to reduce blast radius. Decision needed: greenlight scoped MVP and delay the non-critical optics telemetry sprint by one cycle.

Raj (Eng): If we delay optics telemetry, we can reassign two engineers for 5 weeks. That matches the 6–8 week ask. We'll need a canary plan and an emergency fallback to single-model routing.

Maya (Sales): If we can commit to the scoped MVP and a rollout plan with canary + rollback, I can push to get an LOI. FinCo wants a named date for pilot start.

Priya (CS): Add to acceptance: runbook for failover and a test harness for simulated tenant load. CS will own the runbook.

Noah (Design): I'll mock the console toggle today and hand off a simple CSS-free UI for the pilot.

Jordan (CTO): Ok — conditional go: greenlight if Eng + PM sign up to the timeline and we provide a customer-facing risk doc. Otherwise we give a realistic 'we can start in Q3' answer.

Ava (PM): Vote: 
- Raj: do we have bandwidth to commit to MVP and canary plan?

Raj (Eng): +1 from Eng if we reassign two ICs and push optics telemetry. We'll need support from Eng-SRE for autoscale testing.

Maya (Sales): I'll tell FinCo we can do an 8-week pilot with scoped features, canary rollout, and a signed risk acknowledgment.

Priya (CS): I'll draft the runbook and compliance checklist by Friday.

Liam (SE): I'll prepare the test harness and baseline load script. Sharing early config snippet:
```
route_policy:
  - name: low-latency
    max_latency_ms: 50
    fallback: standard
  - name: standard
    max_latency_ms: 250
```

Ava (PM): Great — next steps:
- Raj to confirm resource reassignments by EOD
- Noah to link mockups in thread
- Priya + Liam to pair on runbook/test harness
- Maya to soft-commit LOI with the 8-week pilot

deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline queued for branch: feature/tenant-cap-shim (no prod deploy until canary sign-off).

Ava (PM): Thanks everyone — we'll regroup tomorrow 10am PT to finalize the customer-facing doc. :thumbsup:
